{{Article header|deck=A cargo commodity that can be bought or laser-mined and is used for Lei Cheung's Engineering workshop unlock.}}

{{Callout|type=tip|label=Quick answer|1=Gold can be bought from suitable '''Extraction''' and '''Refinery''' markets or obtained by laser mining '''metallic rings'''. EDFM has no documented Gold-specific hotspot, so prospect a suitable metallic ring instead. Mined fragments must be processed through a [[Refinery]] before they become cargo. Gold is also required for [[Lei Cheung]]'s '''200-tonne''' workshop unlock at [[Trader's Rest]] in [[Laksak]].<ref name="wiki-miner">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Miner Miner], Elite Dangerous Wiki.</ref><ref name="inara-gold">[https://inara.cz/elite/commodity/42/ Gold — Commodity], Inara.</ref><ref name="journal">[https://hosting.zaonce.net/community/journal/v37/Journal_Manual_v37.pdf Elite Dangerous Journal Manual, version 37], Frontier Developments, “MiningRefined”.</ref><ref name="inara-lei">[https://inara.cz/elite/engineer/10/ Lei Cheung — Engineer], INARA.</ref>}}

{{Commodity infobox|gold}}

'''Gold''' is a market-traded metal and a cargo commodity in ''Elite Dangerous''. It is used in jewellery, luxury goods, and electronics contacts. Commanders can buy it at commodity markets or obtain it by laser mining metallic rings.<ref name="wiki-gold">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Gold Gold], Elite Dangerous Wiki.</ref><ref name="inara-gold" /> Gold recovered from mining must be processed through a [[Refinery]] before it becomes cargo.<ref name="journal" /> Gold is required for [[Lei Cheung]]'s workshop unlock, but it is not an [[Engineering Materials|Engineering Material]] and is not stored in the Engineering Materials inventory.<ref name="inara-lei" />

== Acquisition ==

* '''Buy''' — '''Where:''' suitable commodity markets at '''Extraction''' and '''Refinery''' economy stations.<ref name="inara-gold" /> '''Requirements:''' credits, cargo racks, and enough free cargo space. '''Refinery:''' no; purchased Gold is already cargo.<ref name="journal" /> '''Notes:''' stock and prices change, so check current listings before travelling; delivery distance still matters.
* '''Laser mine''' — '''Where:''' '''Metallic''' rings in an asteroid belt or planetary ring.<ref name="wiki-gold" /><ref name="wiki-miner" /> '''Requirements:''' [[Mining Laser]], [[Prospector Limpet Controller]], collection equipment, cargo racks, and a ship [[Refinery]]. '''Refinery:''' yes; mined fragments must be processed before they become cargo.<ref name="journal" /><ref name="wiki-miner" /> '''Notes:''' no named Gold hotspot is currently documented; prospect a suitable ring instead. A [[Rhino]] is not required for conventional asteroid mining.<ref name="wiki-miner" />

=== Buying Gold ===

Extraction and Refinery economy stations are the market types EDFM currently documents as Gold producers.<ref name="inara-gold" /> That describes a type of economy, not a guarantee that every station will have Gold in stock: availability, demand, and prices change. Check a current [https://inara.cz/elite/commodity/42/ Gold market listing] before travelling, then compare the purchase with your available cargo capacity and the delivery distance.

Buying Gold does not require a refinery; purchased Gold arrives as ordinary cargo. A delivery run still needs enough free cargo space for the quantity you intend to carry, and a longer route can change whether buying is worthwhile.

=== Mining Gold ===

The documented mining method for Gold is '''laser mining in Metallic rings'''. Fit a [[Mining Laser]], [[Prospector Limpet Controller]], collection equipment, a ship [[Refinery]], and cargo racks. Prospect asteroids for Gold, extract the fragments with the laser, collect them, and process them through the refinery before treating them as cargo. See [[How to Laser Mine]] for the full procedure.<ref name="wiki-gold" /><ref name="wiki-miner" /><ref name="journal" />

EDFM's available reference material does not identify a named Gold-specific hotspot. That is not a claim that no hotspot exists; it means that no reliable Gold hotspot is currently documented here. Prospecting a suitable metallic ring is therefore the practical approach rather than searching for a Gold-labelled hotspot.<ref name="wiki-miner" /> A [[Rhino]] is not required for this conventional ship-based asteroid-mining route.

== Uses and Engineering ==

{{Commodity uses|gold}}

For cargo purposes, the 200-unit entry above means a '''200-tonne''' Gold delivery.

=== Lei Cheung's workshop unlock ===

'''Gold is ordinary cargo used as a delivery requirement, not an Engineering Material.''' [[Lei Cheung]] requires '''200 tonnes of Gold''' to unlock his workshop at [[Trader's Rest]] in [[Laksak]].<ref name="inara-lei" /> The donation can be supplied with purchased or mined Gold; if it was mined, the fragments must first be refined into cargo. Gold is carried in the normal cargo hold and is not stored in the separate [[Engineering Materials]] inventory. The 200-tonne requirement needs 200 tonnes of free cargo capacity if delivered in one trip, although it can be split across multiple trips.

For ordinary trading, compare current buying and selling prices, available stock, cargo capacity, and route distance rather than assuming that every Extraction or Refinery station offers the same deal.<ref name="inara-gold" />
